events.text: Moyeon, the archivist who met you at the top of the stairs, walks you through the Scroll Hall of the Jade Court. The shelves go up into cloud. "Everyone who climbs brings a method from below," she says, "and everyone finds it drowns up here. The air is too rich for it. So we start you again, at the bottom. It is not an insult. I started there too."

choices.text: Thank her, and begin at once

effects.log: You sit on the hall floor and breathe the new way until the lamps are lit. Moyeon leaves a cup of tea beside you without a word.

choices.text: Ask what became of her own old method

effects.log: "I still know it," Moyeon says. "I use it to warm my hands in winter. That is all it is good for up here."

choices.text: Ask who wrote the scrolls on the top shelves

effects.log: "People who are not here any more," she says, and looks up for a long moment. "Climb high enough and you may find out."

events.text: A note in a neat hand is waiting in your grotto: "Second shelf. Come before the court sits. M." In the Scroll Hall Moyeon has a scroll ready, tied with a blue cord. "The court has noticed you," she says. "That means I am allowed to give you this. It also means someone at court has started to dislike you. Both are good signs."

choices.text: Take the scroll and practise it

effects.log: The second method moves like the floating isles: never still, never lost. Your energy settles into it at once.
"Nobody important," Moyeon says, too quickly. You take the scroll. She does not meet your eye.
You thank her and put the scroll away for later. Moyeon looks at you as if you had refused a coat in the snow. (The Arts tab, Qi Methods)

events.text: Moyeon takes you past the shelves, through a door you had thought was painted on the wall. Inside is one table and one scroll, the Jade Court's own method, the one its ministers breathe. "I copied this for you myself," she says. "Three nights. If you ever leave the court for a faction that hates it, please do not tell them where you learned to breathe."

effects.log: You promise. The court's method turns your energy with the sky above the sky, and for the first time up here you feel at home.

choices.text: Ask why she copied it herself

effects.log: "Because the clerk who usually does it makes mistakes," Moyeon says, "and I did not want you to have a mistake in your meridians." You take it up.

choices.text: Thank her, and keep your own breath a while

effects.log: You fold the scroll into your sleeve. "It will keep," Moyeon says. "So will I." (The Arts tab, Qi Methods)

events.text: Your faction's elders send for you. In a hall of white jade an old immortal, who has not spoken to you in a hundred years, unrolls a scroll the length of the room. "Rank brings duties," the elder says. "It also brings this. Breathe as we breathe." Behind the elder, half hidden by a pillar, you see Moyeon, who must have been the one to carry it here.

effects.log: The faction's method breathes like a tide of stars: in for an age, out for an age. Moyeon smiles at you from behind the pillar, and is gone.

choices.text: Thank Moyeon first, then the elder

effects.log: The elder raises an eyebrow, and then, surprisingly, laughs. You take the method up. Moyeon goes red to the ears.

choices.text: Take it, but keep your breath for now

effects.log: You bow, take the scroll, and practise nothing yet. The elder says nothing, which up here is a warning. (The Arts tab, Qi Methods)

events.text: Under ten thousand years of moss, in a grotto on a drifting isle, an immortal sits in meditation, and has sat so long that the moss has grown into the folds of the robe. In the lap: a scroll, and a note. "For whoever is patient enough to find me. I was not patient enough to climb higher." When you bring the scroll to Moyeon her hands shake. "This one was lost before the court was built," she says.

effects.log: The lost method opens in your meridians like a door nobody has used in ten thousand years. Somewhere a little dust falls.
You lay the old immortal under the pine of the isle before you read a single line. Then you take the method up, and it is kind to you.

choices.text: Give a copy to the Scroll Hall

effects.log: You let Moyeon copy it for the hall. "Nobody does this," she says. "Nobody." Then you take it up yourself.

events.text: At the top of your faction there is no one left to give you anything, so they give you what the founders left. The hall empties. The scroll on the table was written, they say, by the first immortal who ever sat on the jade throne. Moyeon is not allowed in. She waits at the door all night anyway.

effects.log: By dawn you breathe like the first immortal. When you come out Moyeon is asleep on the step, and you do not wake her.

choices.text: Bring Moyeon in, rule or no rule

effects.log: You open the door. "You will be in trouble," she says, and comes in. You read the founders' method together, and practise it.

choices.text: Leave it on the table for now

effects.log: You touch the scroll and leave it. Some things should wait. (The Arts tab, Qi Methods)

events.text: Behind a waterfall that falls upward, at the end of a cave that is warm when nothing up here is warm, there is a throne of bare rock, and on it a scroll that glows like the first light of morning. Nobody has sat here in longer than the Jade Court has existed. When you tell Moyeon, she sits down on the floor of the Scroll Hall and does not speak for a long time.

choices.text: Take up the oldest method above the clouds

effects.log: The oldest breath above the clouds fills you. For a moment you can feel every isle in the sky turning.

choices.text: Leave the throne as you found it

effects.log: You take the scroll and leave the throne bare, for whoever comes next. You practise the method, and it is gentle.

events.text: The Lamp-Bearer walks you down a road of slow gold to a hall where the new gods learn to be gods. Its lamp swings as it walks; where the light falls you can see your own meridians, as if you were made of glass. "Your immortal breath was a good breath," it says. "It was made for clouds. You are above them now."

effects.log: The god's breath catches like a fire in a new hearth: carefully, and once. It will not go out now.

choices.text: Ask the Lamp-Bearer what it was before

effects.log: "A lamp," it says. "Someone forgot to blow me out." You cannot tell whether it is joking.

choices.text: Ask whether Moyeon will remember you

effects.log: "Everyone who copies a scroll for someone remembers them," the Lamp-Bearer says. You are glad, and you breathe.

events.text: The Lamp-Bearer finds you at the edge of your domain, where your world is still new and thin. It holds its lamp up to the place where your domain stops. "You are weaving it," it says, "but with your hands. Weave it with your breath." It gives you the second method, written in light on nothing.

effects.log: Each breath is a thread now, and each thread is the world.
"Somebody helped me," says the Lamp-Bearer, "and I have never been able to pay them back." You take it up.
The light-written method waits in the air of your domain until you want it. (The Arts tab, Qi Methods)

events.text: The pantheons, who agree on nothing, agree on one method: the one they all breathe. A council sends it to you by the Lamp-Bearer, who carries it as carefully as fire. "They argued for an age about whether you deserved it," it says. "Then they gave it to you to stop arguing."

effects.log: You breathe the one thing the gods have never fought over, and your domain grows quieter, and stronger.
"Everyone, at first," says the Lamp-Bearer. "Then fewer." You take the method up.
You let the method rest for now. The gods will notice; they notice everything. (The Arts tab, Qi Methods)

events.text: As a General of Heaven you are given what the court gives its generals: a seat by the ancient hearth, where the first fire of the gods is kept by the oldest of them. The keeper is so old its face is only light. It teaches you the hearth's breath without a word.

effects.log: The first fire of the gods settles into your meridians. You will never be cold again, in any world.
The keeper says a name that is older than names. The Lamp-Bearer, waiting by the door, bows very low. You take up the method.

choices.text: Sit by the fire, but keep your breath

effects.log: You sit by the hearth for a century and learn nothing on purpose. The keeper does not mind. (The Arts tab, Qi Methods)

events.text: In a ruin of gold between two stars lies a god nobody prays to any more. It is not dead; gods do not die, they are forgotten. It opens one eye. "You remembered to look," it says. "Then take what I was." Its method is the dark before the first day.

choices.text: Take it, and promise to remember the god

effects.log: You take up the forgotten god's method, and say its name aloud once a year after. Somewhere, it is a little less forgotten.
The forgotten god closes its eye. Its method is yours. The ruin is quieter when you leave.

events.text: There is a method the gods do not teach, because it was never written: the breath at the root of the Dao, where the realms grow from. The Lamp-Bearer takes you to the root, and then, for the first time, sets its lamp down. "I cannot go further," it says. "I am only a lamp."

effects.log: At the root of the Dao you breathe the way the realms breathe. When you come back the Lamp-Bearer is waiting, and its light is brighter.
You pick up the lamp and carry it to the root. The Lamp-Bearer, without its lamp, laughs for the first time in an age. You breathe the root's breath.

events.text: Where the stars are born there is a womb of light, and in it the last breath of a god who made the first stars. It is waiting the way seeds wait. The Lamp-Bearer will not come near it. "That is older than every pantheon," it says. "Older than me. Be careful."

effects.log: You breathe where the stars are born, and nothing in you will grow old for an age of ages.
You take the method and leave the light as it was. The Lamp-Bearer is visibly relieved, which is hard for a lamp.

events.text: The Jade Spring is a small pool at the foot of the cloud stairs, so clear it looks empty. Its keeper, Danbi, is an old immortal with a bucket in each hand and moss on her shoes. "Most people who come here do not say why," she says. "I always know anyway."

choices.text: Tell her about the voice in your heart

effects.log: Danbi nods as if you had told her the weather. "It always talks the most just before it lets go," she says.
Danbi hums while you bathe. It is the only sound for a mile.

events.text: The water goes grey around you, then black, as the spring finds the demonic qi in your meridians. Danbi puts down her buckets. "It can take it," she says. "All of it. The art you built on it goes with it. Or you can climb out now, and keep it, and come back next year to quiet the heart again. It is your qi."

choices.text: Let the spring take the dark qi

effects.log: You stay in the water until it boils black and clears.
You climb out before the spring can finish. The dark qi stays; the heart is quieter for now.

choices.text: Ask Danbi what she would do

effects.log: "Keep what you need," she says. "Burn what you do not." She does not say which is which.

events.text: One evening Danbi sits on the edge of the spring with her feet in the water, which you had thought would kill a person. "I came up the stairs as a demon," she says. "Ten thousand deaths in my meridians. The spring took them. It took everything else with them: my art, my name, my fear. I stayed to carry the water. It seemed fair."

effects.log: You sit with your feet in the cold until you cannot feel them, and Danbi tells you the rest. You never repeat it.

choices.text: Tell her your own worst year

effects.log: You tell her. Danbi listens the way the spring does, taking it in and giving nothing back but quiet.

events.text: A god comes down from the Divine Realm to bathe in the Jade Spring, which Danbi says happens about once an age. It is the god of something sad; you can tell from the way the water goes still around it. Danbi hands it a towel as if it were anyone.

choices.text: Bow, and leave it the water

effects.log: The god nods to you on its way out. "Thank you," it says, "for not asking." Danbi says that was very well done.
You keep bathing. The god, after a while, smiles. It is a sad smile, but a real one.

events.text: Two cranes land at the far side of the Jade Spring and drink, and do not seem to mind you at all. Danbi says they come every spring, though there are no seasons up here. "They keep their own," she says.

effects.log: The cranes drink, preen, and go. You feel lighter than they look.
You carry water while the cranes watch. Danbi pretends not to be pleased.
